forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Worcester Council behind on five audit recommendations on spending controls
news_drafts.lead: Worcester Council's Audit and Governance Committee was told the council has 19 outstanding internal audit recommendations, of which 5 are overdue. The overdue findings cover transparency code publication, reporting of purchasing card spending, and contract management monitoring. The council has implemented 74 per cent of recommendations overall, just below its 75 per cent target. The recommendations follow audits of the council's financial controls and procurement processes.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appx 1 Internal Audit Progress Report WCC

findings.paper_title: Appx 1 Internal Audit Progress Report WCC
findings.headline: Five audit recommendations are overdue across financial controls, procurement and transparency areas
findings.detail: The council has 19 outstanding audit recommendations, of which 5 are overdue. These cover Transparency Code publication requirements (2 findings), Purchasing Cards expenditure reporting (1 finding), and Contract Management KPI monitoring (2 findings). The council's overall recommendation implementation rate is 74%, just below the 75% target.
findings.matters: Overdue audit recommendations indicate the council is not promptly addressing identified control gaps. Delays in implementing recommendations on financial controls and procurement could affect the reliability of financial reporting and expose the council to operational risk.
findings.figures: 5 of 19 outstanding recommendations overdue; implementation rate 74% against 75% target
findings.quote: There are 19 outstanding internal audit recommendations; however, and 5 of these are overdue.

findings.headline: Large £6.957m crematorium refurbishment project proceeding on budget to October 2026 completion
findings.detail: Astwood Crematorium refurbishment and replacement cremators project is the largest single capital investment at £6.957m total cost. Funded by £1m Salix environmental grant with £3.296m prudential borrowing in 2026/27. Project remains on budget and is expected to complete in October 2026, demonstrating successful delivery of major capital projects in contrast to delays and cost pressures on regeneration schemes.
findings.matters: Demonstrates council can deliver large capital projects on schedule and budget, providing positive signal on project management capability
findings.figures: Total cost £6.957m, Salix grant £1m, 2026/27 borrowing £3.296m, Expected completion October 2026, Currently on budget
findings.quote: The total budget is £6.957m and is funded from Salix Grant £1m with the remainder being supported through prudential borrowing. The project is expected to be completed in October 2026 and is currently on budget.

findings.headline: LAHF housing acquisitions for temporary accommodation financed by borrowing dependent on rental income
findings.detail: Council is using Local Authority Housing Fund grant (£243.6k in 2026/27) matched with 50-60% council funding through prudential borrowing to purchase housing for temporary accommodation and refugee resettlement. Council has purchased 9 dwellings to date; 2 purchased this year using £165k grant and £184k borrowing. Financial sustainability depends entirely on rental income covering property repairs, maintenance, and debt service costs.
findings.matters: Yield-based borrowing model creates direct link between occupancy rates and debt serviceability; shortfalls in rental income would impair ability to service debt
findings.figures: LAHF grant 2026/27: £243.6k, Match funding through borrowing: 50-60% of grant, Recent purchases: 2 dwellings with £165k grant + £184k borrowing
findings.quote: The level of rent covers property repairs and maintenance and borrowing costs.

findings.headline: Prudential borrowing increased by £4.1m to £10.6m to finance expanded capital programme
findings.detail: Original approved borrowing of £6.467m has increased to £10.603m (71% increase) in the revised programme. Major borrowing allocations include £3.296m for crematorium refurbishment, £4.028m for Future High Streets projects, £710k for Barrington House temporary accommodation property, and £362k for housing acquisitions. Borrowing now finances 39% of the total £27.3m capital programme.
findings.matters: Material increase in capital borrowing affects council's debt position and impacts future borrowing capacity
findings.quote: The project includes the refurbishment of Astwood Crematorium and replacement cremators. The total budget is £6.957m and is funded from Salix Grant £1m with the remainder being supported through prudential borrowing.

findings.headline: Scala Theatre and Corn Exchange projects showing £596k combined cost overruns and slipping to 2027
findings.detail: Future High Streets-funded Scala Theatre is not completing until early 2027, with forecast overspend of £224k against budget of £4,943k. Corn Exchange Cultural Investment project has forecast overspend of £372k against budget of £3,706k, with public realm works delayed into 2027. Council is requesting additional budget for these schemes in a separate agenda item. The combined overspend on these two flagship regeneration projects is the primary driver of overall capital forecast pressure.
findings.matters: Cost overruns and schedule delays on major regeneration projects indicate project management challenges and financing risks that could affect future capital capability
findings.figures: FHSF project: budget £4,943k, forecast £5,167k, variance £224k; Cultural project: budget £3,706k, forecast £4,078k, variance £372k
findings.quote: Forecast spend for 2026/27 is £27.429m, and net pressure of £0.163m mainly relating to additional costs of the Public Arts Venue at the Scala Theatre and Corn Exchange
